newsitem.title: UK: Tioxide says ready for full independence.
newsitem.headline: Tioxide says ready for full independence.

text.p: One of the world's biggest pigment manufacturers, ICI Plc-owned Tioxide Group Ltd, said on Thursday it welcomed the opportunity of greater independence offered by ICI's plan to consider floating the group.

Earlier, in its 1996 results statement, ICI said it would consider a float of the Tioxide company as part of a bid to reduce its group exposure to strongly cyclical markets, a characteristic of its industrial chemicals portfolio.
Tioxide, named after the contraction for its main product, titanium dioxide, "has operated as a distinct entity throughout its history", the pigment company said in a statement.

Tioxide said that since it became a wholly-owned unit of ICI in 1990 it had benefited from what it described as "substantial investments in plant processes, product development and environmental management".

"This period of investment is now substantially complete and processes have been fully instituted together with a comprehensive cost reduction programme which will carry the benefits of these initiatives well into the future irrespective of who owns the business."
Tioxide has over 3,400 employees and plants in Britain, North America, Malaysia, South Africa, France, Spain and Italy.

Although ICI has always had an interest in Tioxide since the company's foundation in 1930, it had other shareholders up until 1990, including a period between 1978 and 1990 when Cookson Group and ICI held 50 percent each and allowed the firm to operate as a public company. Looking ahead, Tioxide said it had major programmes underway to enhance its competitive position in the industry, where it considers itself to be the largest producer of titanium dioxide-based pigments in Europe and number two in the world with about one sixth of world capacity.

If Tioxide were to float it would be a slightly more concentrated industry investment play than Millennium Chemicals Inc, the newly-floated former Hanson Plc unit, whose business includes the world number three tioxide producer SCM but also polyethylene market giant Quantum.
In busy trading of ICI shares after the group's results and news of its demerger thoughts, the stock fell by 3-1/2 pence to 761 pence by 0950 GMT, broadly in line with the overall market.
